t.p: Edo period onward (wide ripsaws from 1763); higonokami 1896–present
t.d: Miki smithing tradition of carpentry blades—saws, chisels, planes, knives and large construction tools.

t.auth: laminated hard-steel edge on softer iron; smith's stamp

t.d: Natural Japanese waterstones (tennen toishi) quarried for finishing blades, used wet.
t.tech: quarried and cut stone used with water

t.mat: cattle horn, wood, aluminium; stainless or carbon steel (XC75, XC100)
t.auth: 'Laguiole' is a generic name, not a protected one; French makers often stamp their mark and steel type on the blade.

t.p: 14th century to present; first steel razors 1680

t.auth: maker and 'Sheffield' tang stamps such as 'Warranted Cast Steel'; Cutlers' Company marks

t.mat: X50CrMoV15 stainless, carbon steels, POM and wood handles
t.auth: 'Solingen' is a protected origin mark; forged full tang, maker's trident/twins stamps

t.d: Swedish forges making hand-forged axes, each signed by its smith.

t.p: Carpentry first developed in the 12th century
